Hi! Let's count triangular numbers, and watch a little triangle turn into a working number pattern.
The small letter n tells us how many rows to use. The big answer tells us how many dots belong to one triangle.
Make two matching triangles, fit them into a rectangle, then choose one of the two equal groups. Watch the formula move!
one times two, divided by two, equals
two times three, divided by two, equals
three times four, divided by two, equals
four times five, divided by two, equals
Look again. One, two, three, and four dots make the rows. Turn a matching copy around and slide it into the spaces.
Together they make four rows of five. Dividing by two means choosing one of these two equal triangles, with every dot kept whole.
five times six, divided by two, equals
A new row joins the bottom. This row has five dots, so the triangle grows by five. The row number and the total are different.
six times seven, divided by two, equals
seven times eight, divided by two, equals
eight times nine, divided by two, equals
nine times ten, divided by two, equals
ten times eleven, divided by two, equals
The dots will look smaller as more rows fit on screen. Every dot still counts as one. Watch the row labels and the formula.
eleven times twelve, divided by two, equals
twelve times thirteen, divided by two, equals
thirteen times fourteen, divided by two, equals
fourteen times fifteen, divided by two, equals
Our answer now has three digits. The rule stays the same: two matching triangles, one rectangle, and one of its two equal groups.
